drugs_and_rules: PDL footnotes exclude Wegovy for weight reduction and Zepbound for weight reduction without sleep apnea, per a secondary reading of the July 2026 PDL. HJR162 (Mar 5, 2026) asks Medicaid to study the cost of coverage.
latest_change: Legislature asks Medicaid to study GLP-1 costs (HJR162)

drugs_and_rules: Weight control is excluded by regulation (7 AAC 105.110 and 7 AAC 120.112). Wegovy needs BMI 25 or more with heart disease or MASH; Zepbound needs BMI 30 or more with sleep apnea.
AHCCCS policy AMPM 310-V lists medications used for weight loss as a pharmacy benefit exclusion, for managed care plans and fee-for-service.
The pharmacy program states it does not cover medications for weight loss (DUR memo, May 13, 2026). Wegovy is covered for heart risk and MASH; Zepbound for sleep apnea only.
latest_change: Wegovy tablets added to the heart-risk criteria

drugs_and_rules: Adult weight-loss coverage ended Jan 1, 2026 under the 2025-26 Budget Act, in fee-for-service and all managed care plans. Members under 21 are reviewed under EPSDT. Zepbound and Saxenda were removed from the drug list. SB 1089 (signed Sep 28, 2026) lets the state seek a GLP-1 pricing partnership if lawmakers fund it, aiming at or below 2025 Medi-Cal prices; it does not restore Medi-Cal weight-loss coverage.
latest_change: Wegovy for MASH no longer needs PA (weight-loss coverage ended Jan 1, 2026)

drugs_and_rules: Appendix P (Oct 1, 2026) states that medications prescribed for weight loss are not a covered benefit.
No GLP-1s for weight loss. Since June 1, 2025 the state plan (SPA 25-0014) covers only orlistat and phentermine for weight loss. Wegovy is not covered for weight management alone.
latest_change: Wegovy added for MASH; Wegovy claims need a heart or MASH diagnosis

drugs_and_rules: Wegovy, Zepbound, Saxenda and liraglutide with PA: BMI 30 or more, or 27 to under 30 with a weight-related condition, plus diet and activity. Renewal needs 5% weight loss.
latest_change: state PA form revised (weight management, MASH and heart risk)

drugs_and_rules: Fee-for-service excludes anti-obesity drugs (2023 provider manual), but MedStar Family Choice DC, one of two managed care plans, lists Wegovy and Zepbound with PA; the uses it approves were not found.
latest_change: Wellpoint DC members moved to AmeriHealth Caritas DC

drugs_and_rules: Weight control medications are a non-covered category. Heart and sleep apnea cells are per one managed care plan's policy (Aetna Better Health of Florida, Sep 1, 2026); AHCA criteria for those uses were not found.
wegovy_heart_risk: Covered with PA (per one managed care plan's policy)
zepbound_sleep_apnea: Covered with PA (per one managed care plan's policy)

drugs_and_rules: No adult GLP-1 weight-loss coverage. Saxenda and Xenical are listed only for ages 12 to 17 (PDL Oct 1, 2026).
latest_change: weight management class reviewed, no changes

drugs_and_rules: Plan by plan. The findings in a 2026 Senate bill say the state excludes GLP-1s for obesity in most situations, and the AlohaCare and UnitedHealthcare QUEST plans exclude weight-loss drugs; the other three plans were not checked. 2026 bills to lift the exclusion failed.
latest_change: 2026 session: bills to require coverage (SB 3195, HB 2456) failed

drugs_and_rules: The PDL (July 1, 2026) has no weight-loss class and no Wegovy or Zepbound rows, and GLP-1s need a type 2 diabetes diagnosis. No written weight-loss exclusion was found in rule IDAPA 16.03.09.662.
Wegovy and Zepbound are not covered for weight loss alone (PDL Oct 1, 2026).
wegovy_heart_risk: Covered with PA (heart risk and MASH only)

drugs_and_rules: Wegovy and Zepbound are not covered exclusively for weight loss (PA criteria Dec 1, 2025). On Jul 30, 2026 the governor said Medicaid will cover select GLP-1s for obesity through the BALANCE model; the state said eligibility criteria and timing would be announced later, and we found no state notice setting them as of Oct 28, 2026.
Weight loss is an excluded use under the Iowa State Plan (PA form 470-0058, January 2026).

Wegovy, Zepbound, Saxenda and Foundayo with PA: BMI 30 or more, or 27 with a weight-related condition, plus a lifestyle plan. A stricter high-cost rule (BMI 40 and 3 months of lifestyle change) does not apply to Zepbound (since Apr 1, 2024) or Wegovy (since Jun 1, 2025) but still lists Saxenda and Foundayo. Criteria reviewed Aug 19, 2026.
latest_change: Wegovy exempted from the high-cost BMI 40 rule

drugs_and_rules: Regulation 907 KAR 23:010 excludes drugs used for weight loss unless the outpatient drug list covers them, and the Wegovy criteria list only heart risk and MASH.
zepbound_sleep_apnea: Covered with PA (after a 3-month PAP trial, unless PAP is not tolerated or contraindicated)

drugs_and_rules: No general obesity coverage today. Act 898 of 2026 (SB 433) requires Medicaid to cover medically necessary FDA-approved weight-loss drugs, with criteria set by LDH, prior authorization allowed and step therapy barred. That coverage takes effect only when the Legislature passes an act appropriating money for it; a House amendment replaced the Jan 1, 2027 start in the Senate-passed bill. We found no such appropriation or LDH notice as of Oct 28, 2026.
latest_change: Act 898 signed; coverage waits on funding

drugs_and_rules: MaineCare policy does not allow coverage for weight-loss products. LD 480, a bill to add coverage, died in 2025.
latest_change: DUR Board added Zepbound for sleep apnea

drugs_and_rules: COMAR 10.09.03.05 excludes agents used for weight control. The fee-for-service PDL (July 1, 2026) lists no Wegovy, Zepbound or Foundayo; managed care formularies were not checked.
latest_change: draft state drug board paper recommends joining BALANCE

drugs_and_rules: Weight-loss coverage ended July 3, 2026 per MassHealth (news reports said July 1), in every plan type. Remaining uses need PA and Wegovy is the sole preferred drug. Members under 21 are reviewed under EPSDT.
zepbound_sleep_apnea: Covered with PA, after a Wegovy trial

drugs_and_rules: Since Jan 1, 2026: BMI 40 or more, trial of five older weight-loss drug types, and only to avoid bariatric surgery. Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda with PA; renewal needs 5% loss.
latest_change: limited to BMI 40 or more; Nov 1, 2026 (scheduled): Foundayo added

drugs_and_rules: The Jan 2026 PDL lists Wegovy, Saxenda and Zepbound as weight management drugs, with Wegovy and Saxenda shown as preferred and Zepbound as non-preferred; PA applies. The current BMI and renewal rules on the state PA page could not be read; that page changed Aug 4, 2026.
latest_change: bill to end coverage (HF4142) laid over

drugs_and_rules: Wegovy, Zepbound, Saxenda and Foundayo preferred with PA: BMI 30 or more, or 27 to 29 with a weight-related condition. Renewal needs 5% loss. Since July 2026 adult claims with an obesity code can be approved electronically.
latest_change: criteria list Foundayo; electronic approval for adults

drugs_and_rules: Zepbound preferred with PA: BMI 30 or more, or 27 with a weight-related condition; ages 12 to 17 by BMI percentile. Wegovy is not covered for weight loss. Coverage began Jan 9, 2025.
latest_change: obesity criteria revision proposed; PA form dated Jan 2026

drugs_and_rules: Drugs used for weight loss are listed as non-covered.
zepbound_sleep_apnea: Covered with PA (AHI 15+ while on PAP)

drugs_and_rules: DHHS excludes drugs prescribed for weight control or appetite suppression. The sleep apnea cell is per one managed care plan's policy (Nebraska Total Care); the state form was not opened.
zepbound_sleep_apnea: Covered with PA (per one managed care plan's policy)

drugs_and_rules: The Medicaid Services Manual excludes agents used for weight management, per a secondary reading (the manual itself could not be opened).
No coverage when prescribed solely for weight loss since Jan 1, 2026 (provider notice Oct 9, 2025), naming Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound.
zepbound_sleep_apnea: Covered for severe OSA (PA rules not reviewed)

drugs_and_rules: N.J.A.C. 10:51-1.13 excludes antiobesity agents when used for obesity, except lipase inhibitors such as orlistat.
The Health Care Authority lists Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound as not covered for weight reduction.
NYRx excludes drugs used for weight loss under SSA 1927(d)(2) (pharmacy manual, September 2026). The heart-risk rule asks for BMI over 40, far above the FDA label.

Restored Dec 12, 2025 under the criteria in place Sep 30, 2025: prior approval, BMI 30 or more, or 27 with a weight-related condition, plus lifestyle changes; renewal needs 5% loss. Wegovy preferred, Zepbound and Saxenda non-preferred at reinstatement. Sources disagree on October 2026: one managed care plan lists Zepbound and Foundayo as preferred from Oct 1, 2026, while the state drug list notes the Zepbound vial was removed from the obesity class Sep 4, 2026. Coverage had ended Oct 1, 2025. A 2026 law (Session Law 2026-1, signed Apr 30, 2026) told the state to send lawmakers a plan by Oct 1, 2026 letting Medicaid health plans manage weight-loss use, such as requiring nutrition and lifestyle programs, starting no earlier than July 1, 2027; coverage for diabetes and heart disease cannot change.
Weight-loss coverage is limited to phentermine, bupropion, naltrexone and topiramate; no GLP-1 is covered for weight loss.
wegovy_heart_risk: Covered with PA (ages 55 to 74, after Ozempic or Rybelsus)

drugs_and_rules: Ohio Administrative Code rule 5160-9-03 excludes drugs for the treatment of obesity.
latest_change: P&T committee recommended Wegovy as preferred with PA in a new non-obesity class

drugs_and_rules: Wegovy is not approved without established heart disease and Zepbound is not approved without sleep apnea (PA criteria, Oct 1, 2026).
Drugs prescribed only for weight management are not covered for adults; under 21, case-by-case review.
Coverage for overweight and obesity ended Jan 1, 2026 for adults 21 and older, in fee-for-service and managed care. Under 21 is reviewed under EPSDT. Saxenda is not covered for any use.
latest_change: weight-loss coverage ended; earlier PAs expired Dec 31, 2025

drugs_and_rules: Foundayo, Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound are not covered when prescribed solely for weight loss from Oct 1, 2026, under the state fiscal 2027 budget. Under 21: EPSDT review.
Coverage began Nov 1, 2024 and ended Jan 1, 2026; obesity GLP-1s were removed from the PDL Dec 31, 2025. Diabetes coverage continues.
The pharmacy manual lists agents used for weight loss as non-covered.

Wegovy and Zepbound preferred, Saxenda non-preferred, with PA: BMI 30 or more, or 27 with a weight-related condition, plus nutrition and lifestyle changes. Renewal needs 5% loss. Coverage began Aug 1, 2025.
zepbound_sleep_apnea: Covered with PA (after 3 months of CPAP or BiPAP)

drugs_and_rules: Weight management drugs outside specific exceptions are not covered for traditional Medicaid clients 21 and over.
A one-year fee-for-service weight-loss pilot that began July 1, 2025 ended June 30, 2026. The PA form said coverage may not continue past that date; we found no state notice of the end.
The PDL (Oct 2, 2026) lists drugs used for weight loss as a policy exclusion.

BMI over 40, or over 37 with dyslipidemia, hypertension or type 2 diabetes, after trying a non-GLP-1 weight-loss drug and the preferred product. Wegovy, Zepbound, Saxenda and Foundayo; renewals stop below BMI 25.
latest_change: new form adds Foundayo and Wegovy tablets

drugs_and_rules: Apple Health policies say Wegovy and Zepbound are not covered for weight loss; the Wegovy policy cites WAC 182-530-2100 and SSA 1927(d)(2)(A).
Agents used for weight loss are a benefit exclusion.
New weight management class from July 1, 2026: Zepbound and Foundayo preferred, PA for every drug. BMI 30 or more, or 27 to under 30 with two or more risk factors. Saxenda and older drugs dropped.
The 2024 provider manual (Revision 26) excludes “anorexiant products” for all Medicaid plans, and the June 2026 criteria require heart disease for Wegovy and sleep apnea for Zepbound.
